Title: Deep Vein Thrombosis Hits 900,000 Americans a Year — Is Your Desk Job Putting You at Risk?

Description:
If you've landed after a long flight or road trip with one leg swollen and achy, that could be deep vein thrombosis — a clot forming deep in your leg. The CDC estimates it affects up to 900,000 Americans every year, and up to 100,000 people die from it, the third leading cause of cardiovascular death after heart attack and stroke.

Your calf muscles pump blood back to your heart with every step. Sit too long, especially in a cramped seat or at a desk, and that pump stops — blood pools and can clot.

Three habits cut your risk the most: moving every hour, staying hydrated instead of reaching for coffee or alcohol, and wearing compression socks on long trips.

Sudden swelling in just one leg, or shortness of breath, needs an ER visit right away.
